name: Just One

source.title: Just One English rules (2025), retailer-hosted copy

setup.text: Shuffle the cards and make a face-down deck of 13 random cards in the middle. The rest stay in the box.
Take an easel, an erasable pencil of the same colour and a cloth.

by_count.3: Take two easels, except the active player who takes one.
by_count.4: Take two easels, except the active player who takes one.

setup.text: Pick a random player to be the first active player.

turn.summary: The cooperative group helps the active player guess a secret word by writing one-word clues. Matching clues cancel.
steps: Select: the active player takes the top card without looking and stands it on their easel facing the others, then names a number from 1 to 5. That word is the Mystery Word.
Write clues: everyone but the active player secretly writes one valid single-word clue on their easel.
Compare: the active player closes their eyes. The others show easels and cancel identical or invalid clues, laying those easels down.
Guess: the active player opens their eyes and makes one guess from the remaining clues, or passes.
End of round: erase clues. The player to the left becomes the active player.

round_end: Correct guess: place the card face up beside the deck.
Pass: the card goes back in the box.
Wrong guess: the card and the top card of the deck both go back in the box. If the deck is empty, remove a won card if you can.
If every clue is cancelled, the Mystery Word card goes in the box and you go straight to the end of the round.
end: The game ends when the 13-card deck is empty.

scoring.text: Count the cards you won out of 13 and read off your level: 0-3 Eek, 4-6 Not bad, 7-8 Average, 9-10 Good, 11 Very good, 12 Impressive, 13 Perfect.

missed.text: If you do not know the Mystery Word, the active player may choose a different number.
Invalid clues are cancelled too: foreign translations, same-family words, made-up words and homophones of the Mystery Word.
Identical clues include same family, singular and plural, and spelling mistakes.
A wrong guess costs two cards: the Mystery Word and the next card from the deck.
The active player may pass instead of guessing; that loses only the current card.
Valid clues include compound words, proper nouns, numbers, onomatopoeia, acronyms and special characters.

unverified: Player range 3-7 is inferred from the 3 and 4 player variant and the 7 easels listed; the rulebook text gives no explicit range.
